name: Mobility Global, Inc.
one_line_reason: A new S&P Global spin-off (completed 2026-07-01) with 41% EBITDA margins and 7% growth that trades at a discount to data peers, but the stock is up 14% and not hated, so the gap is modest.
evidence: Q3 2026 revenue +7.4% (organic +7.6%) to $478M, CARFAX +8%, B2B +6%, adjusted EBITDA $195M (41% margin), free cash flow $186M (8-K 2026-11-12). The $2.0B dividend to S&P Global was funded with new senior notes, so net debt is about $1.6B (roughly 2x EBITDA). Board authorized an $800M buyback (target $350-450M by end 2027) and a $0.06 quarterly dividend; GAAP net income fell 41% in Q3 on first standalone-company costs and interest. A CFO-level insider (Mark Peek) bought $0.98M at about $19.50 in Aug 2026, right after the spin.
key_numbers: EV/EBITDA about 11x (EV $8.7B / 2026 run-rate EBITDA about $0.78B) vs EFX 12.8x, TRI 19.8x, VRSK 19.5x, SPGI 17.1x; fwd P/E 14.2 vs EFX 18.7, VRSK 23.2; FCF yield 6.5%; no own history (spun 2026-07-01); price $23.93, 1y +14%

name: Honeywell Aerospace Inc.
one_line_reason: The stock fell about 20% on its first standalone report because a shortage of cast and forged parts from a few suppliers capped output and forced a guidance cut; demand and backlog are growing.
evidence: Q3 2026 sales $4.64B (+2% organic), adjusted EBIT $1.16B (+1%), backlog $19.3B (+12%), trailing-12-month orders +9%, free cash flow $500M; full-year EPS and second-half FCF guidance were raised in the 2026-10-28 release after the September cut (EBITDA guide from $4.65-4.75B to $4.35-4.45B) (8-K 2026-10-28). The CEO blamed a small number of mechanical suppliers and said additional sources are being qualified for higher output in 2027. A securities class action covers statements from 2026-06-29 to 2026-09-01. Director Craig Arnold bought $1.0M at $156.00 on 2026-09-01.
